name: Haiku concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Small-cap cyclical momentum with value rotation (TNA, IWD, XLE, XLI, XLF), selective tech exposure, rate hedging via short TLT and low-vol short.
novelty: Shifts from mega-cap AI/enterprise software focus (R1/R2) to small-cap Russell leadership (TNA 18%, IWD 14%) and cyclical sectors (energy, industrials, financials). Uses position-level stops/profit-taking and tactical shorts (TLT, USMV) to manage rotation risk and harvest momentum decay, emphasizing capital efficiency over leverage stacking.

positions.thesis: Russell 2000 3x leverage; small caps +106% YTD with secular outperformance vs mega-cap; runway into H2 2026
Large-cap value rotation; up +29.5% YTD with IWD catching up vs. growth as rates stabilize; dividend yield buffer
Energy +34.1% YTD; commodity tailwind, geopolitical premium, relative undervaluation vs. macro consensus
Industrials +21.7% YTD; cyclical play on infrastructure demand, capex cycles; secular underowned
Financials +11.2% YTD, lagging; rotation opportunity as rates sticky, net interest margin benefits
Emerging markets +37.3% YTD; international cyclical exposure, relative valuation, currency hedge
Nasdaq unleveraged; maintain core tech/growth exposure without leverage fee drag; tactical 5% to limit rotation risk
Nasdaq 3x leverage; tactical if tech momentum sustains, sized to manage 3x volatility and fee burden (5bps leveraged)
20-year bonds short; growth narrative supports lower bond prices, rate pressure from sticky inflation, harvest duration risk
Low-volatility short; tactical hedge against crowding; rotation from defensive to cyclicals should underweight USMV

outlook: Small-cap cyclical momentum sustains into Q3 2026 as Fed pauses rate hikes; energy benefits from persistent geopolitical premium. Financials rotate higher on net interest margin stability. Tech consolidates after run, reducing pressure on rate-sensitive sectors. Crypto remains challenged (avoided). Bond yields stay sticky; TLT short hedges portfolio against growth repricing. Value/cyclical outperformance continues relative to defensive. Position-level stops/TPs manage rotation decay and tail risk. Reassess weekly as macro data (PCE, employment) arrives.
